recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. A separate editorial cleanup could remove the pre-existing 'a the formal URI' wording, but that typo does not alter the FHIR-25888 semantics and is below the reconciliation threshold for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-25888 was a Published FHIR-core ValueSet change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked for ValueSet.expansion.contains.property to support sub-properties by adding subProperty 0..*, subProperty.code 1..1, and subProperty.value[x] 1..1 with the same value datatypes as property.value[x], and by updating the ValueSet/$expand property input text to mention returned subproperties and '*' returning all properties and sub-properties.
initial_application: Git commit ff7b414909e963e85d7204f5dde7f3b4aa1f03a5 directly applied FHIR-25888 by adding the ValueSet subProperty elements and updating source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-expand.xml. Later source history preserved the substantive model and documentation.
additional_context: The final Jira comments and Vocabulary 2022-02-21 minutes revised the solution to make subProperty one level only. They also note that changing ValueSet.expansion.contains.property.code from 1..1 to 0..1 was considered but not recommended for this ticket; the follow-up Zulip thread did not produce a later final decision requiring that cardinality change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active ValueSet source already has property.code 1..1, property.value[x] 1..1, subProperty 0..*, subProperty.code 1..1, and subProperty.value[x] 1..1 using the matching property value datatype set, and the $expand property parameter text already describes returned subproperties and '*' including sub-properties.
